Bounded improvements are demonstrable
Morewedge and colleagues found lasting improvement on tested biases after brief training; Sellier and colleagues later tested transfer to a business decision case with 290 graduate students. These are useful, limited demonstrations that particular reasoning skills can improve. They do not show that the Sequences create exceptional general-purpose competence.
Morewedge et al. (2015); Sellier, Scopelliti & Morewedge (2019)

content:
Specify what would count as less than success
A serious research agenda can begin from the hope that more is possible. It should then name expected improvements, comparison conditions and evidence that would reduce that hope. Otherwise the hopeful reader bears the costs while the promised art is perpetually awaiting its first adequate practitioner.

An aspiration is being used to explain its missing evidence
The absence of spectacular results may reflect insufficient practice, limited transfer, weak methods or an unrealistic target. The essay does not discriminate among those explanations. Continually redefining real rationality as whatever would finally produce awesome results makes the promise immune to ordinary disappointment.
